clue.text: Urban sprawl is about to change with parking introduced

indicators.note: introduced says the letter for parking is brought into the rearranged letters
to change tells you the two words before it must alter their letter order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters of fodder
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A planner predicts the city's outskirts will be transformed once car parks arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about to' reads as one phrase, but only 'is about' is fodder: 'to change' rearranges it to SUBTOIA, and 'introduced' drops P into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage (suburb plus utopia) for monotonous suburban development spreading over the countryside, which is what sprawl of this kind is.

clue.text: Plumber not so inferior?

indicators.note: not tells you the next word, so, is absent from the synonym for plumber

parts.note: to plumb is to sound a depth, so one who plumbs is a sounder
taken as written, the two letters removed

explanation.surface: A tradesman's work is judged to be not all that bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The plumber is no tradesman but someone who plumbs depths, a SOUNDER; 'not so' takes SO away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a preposition or adjective of rank: someone inferior to you is beneath you in the hierarchy.

clue.text: Cast in a mould, a little bird

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small ornamental bird has been made by pouring metal into a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a ground-dwelling South American species resembling a partridge.

clue.text: Put a bloody coat on and have a night out

definitions.meaning: taken literally, giving a place a layer of blood-coloured decoration
the idiom for going out and celebrating boisterously

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a riotous evening of celebration, which read word for word describes covering a place in a crimson coating.

clue.text: Early development of canine tooth (just the tip)

indicators.note: development of suggests the next word's letters evolving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

indicators.note: just the tip takes only the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A dentist notes that a pointed tooth has started to come through ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges CANINE to ANCIEN, and 'just the tip' adds the T of tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the historical sense: early civilisations are those of the distant past.

clue.text: Sort of average community?

parts.note: par is the expected or average standard, as in below par
the suffix -ish means sort of, as in greenish

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood is summed up as pretty middling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'Sort of average' is read whimsically as a word meaning average plus the suffix that means 'sort of'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a local church district and the people living in it.

clue.text: They will be sold off eventually

definitions.text: They will be sold off eventually

parts.words: They will be sold off eventually
parts.note: off is read as gone bad: these are items that will have spoiled by the time they are sold if one waits long enough

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: food and similar stock that decays, so if kept long enough it would be rotten when bought.

clue.text: Surrey town rejected English name — that is right

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole run of pieces after it is read backwards

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
ie abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A town in Surrey turned down an English name, and that was the correct call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole run E, TAG, IE, R (ETAGIER) backwards. The answer is a commuter town south of London in the county of Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a place in that English county, at the foot of the North Downs.

clue.text: Groom doesn't nag — his wife did that!

definitions.note: points at a man known for having a nagging wife

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and arrange, so the following words have their letters put in order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A new husband is no scold, though his bride certainly was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is a verb here, rearranging DOESNT NAG. The answer is a character in the British soap Coronation Street, the idle husband of the famously nagging Hilda.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by allusion: the soap character whose spouse Hilda was forever scolding him.

clue.text: God's a great teacher in this

indicators.note: in places the teacher inside the letters given by a great

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or great
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: The Almighty is hailed as an outstanding instructor in this field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'great' is A1, with the figure 1 written as the letter I, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebrew name for the deity, used in place of the unspoken divine name.

clue.text: Four cuts of meat fair

indicators.note: cuts means the numeral slices into the word for of meat

parts.note: carnal means of the flesh, from the Latin for meat
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A butcher offers four joints at a reasonable price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' is a verb: IV cuts into CARNAL. The fair is a funfair, not a description of the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: a travelling funfair or festival with rides and stalls.

clue.text: Greek god, for me and America

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
taken as written
the US is America, with the article included

explanation.surface: A deity of Greece is claimed on behalf of the speaker and the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Titan of Hellenic myth who stole fire from Olympus for mankind.

clue.text: Uranium found in lead free house?

indicators.note: found in says the uranium symbol sits inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A survey detects radioactive metal in a home said to contain no lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead free' reads as one phrase but splits: lead gives Pb, and a 'free house' in Britain is a bar not tied to one brewery.
explanation.definitionFit: An example, hence the question mark: a free house is a bar independent of any brewery.

clue.text: Have survived being crazy

definitions.meaning: said in the first person, a survivor's report in two short words that they are all right
wild and out of control, as in running berserk

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it is a first-person report of being all right; as one word it means in a frenzied, uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Prioritised cash, should a hotel open

indicators.note: open means these pieces split the word for cash apart and sit inside it

parts.note: bread is slang for money
should means ought to
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone put money first in case a new hotel started trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' has OUGHT TO, A and H prising BREAD apart after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a matter forced to a crisis is one made urgent, pushed to the front of the queue.

clue.text: Artist controlled future date?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
something kept in check is controlled

explanation.surface: A painter managed to fix an appointment for later.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, an offer deferred to a later occasion, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Spits as a result of confinement

definitions.text: Spits as a result of confinement

parts.words: Spits as a result of confinement
parts.note: a spit is an exact likeness, as in spitting image, and confinement is the old word for childbirth: two exact likenesses produced by one birth

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: siblings from a single labour who are each other's exact likeness.

clue.text: It's hard to get up the day before everyone else

parts.note: the eve of an event is the day before it
the rest are all the others

explanation.surface: Rising earlier than the whole household by a full day is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' means climb, not rise from bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the world's highest mountain is famously difficult to climb.

clue.text: Irish town's empty chapel on my left

indicators.note: empty removes the contents of the next word, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: me is the informal or dialect form of my, as in me old mate

explanation.surface: Directions in an Irish town point to a deserted chapel on the left-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves CL from chapel. The answer is the county town of Tipperary.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a place in County Tipperary in Ireland.

clue.text: Who's quiet? A giant

parts.note: who taken as written, the possessive s ignored
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a means per, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is silent, and the answer is a colossus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is not an article here but supplies PER, as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: something enormous of its kind.

clue.text: Fall, when wind comes from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming from the south means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: wind in the digestive sense is gas

explanation.surface: Autumn arrives once the breeze is a southerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes from the south' turns GAS upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to droop or sink downwards.

clue.text: Very good circles and spots

indicators.note: circles means the word for very good goes round the letter for and

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
'n' is the clipped form of and, as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: A design praised for its excellent rings and dots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' is a verb here, ACE going round N; 'and' is not a link but gives the N.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin condition consists of pimples, so it is a breakout of them.

clue.text: In god is sin

parts.note: these five letters are a rearrangement of a word for performing, so a crossword clue for them could be that word with an adjective meaning incorrect as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A stark theological claim that the deity contains evil.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: IN GOD is DOING with its letters out of order, and the answer itself reads as the instruction that produces it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an immoral or illegal act, a transgression.

clue.text: How note becomes not very much

parts.note: the clue's word note turns into not by losing its final letter, so the phrase wanted describes a word whose tail is missing

explanation.surface: A muddled explanation of a tiny amount of money.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer says how NOTE turns into NOT, its last letter going. 'not' belongs to that part, so the definition is 'very much' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that helps immensely is said to help this much.

clue.text: Wire on right secured by band

indicators.note: secured by means the band holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a band of people working together is a team
in cricket the on side is the leg side of the field

explanation.surface: A cable on the right-hand side is held in place by a strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured by' is the container signal. In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field, the one behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: a wire is an old term for a message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Huge game bird

parts.note: OS is the clothing-label abbreviation for outsize
game is animals hunted, which are prey

explanation.surface: An enormous fowl shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a fish-eating raptor.

clue.text: Fish died. Curry did it

definitions.note: refers to John Curry, the British Olympic figure-skating champion of 1976

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish related to rays
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A spicy dish is blamed for killing the pet fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Curry is not food but John Curry, the British figure skater who won Olympic gold in 1976.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by example: gliding on ice was what the Olympic champion John famously did.

clue.text: Final drama school film

parts.note: final means last
RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school

explanation.surface: A student production to end a course at an acting college.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA, the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, is Britain's best-known acting college.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is Fellini's 1954 Italian picture about a travelling strongman.
